definition: An AI boom is a period of rapid growth in the field of artificial intelligence.
details: The most recent boom happened in the 2020s before seeing increased acceleration and media coverage. Generative AI technologies include large language models (LLM), which generate text and code, image models, and video models, and world models. This period is sometimes referred to as an AI spring, a term used to contrast it with previous AI winters. As of 2026, large frontier models have been released by OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Meta Superintelligence Labs, and SpaceXAI in the United States, and by the AI industry in China, including Alibaba Cloud, DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and Z.ai. Many leading models, largely from China, are open weights or open-source; open weights small language models are optimized to run locally on personal computers. These include many models under Alibaba's Qwen, Google's Gemma, Nvidia's Nemotron, and Meta's Muse Glimmer. Key advances preceding precipitating the boom include the transformer (2017), generative pre-trained transformer (2018) and reinforcement learning from human feedback. story: Picture an engineer at a cluttered workbench, turning a clever idea over in their hands until it finally clicks. At its heart it is a simple notion, once you strip away the fancy name. A small key that opens a much bigger door. It is one of those ideas that feels obvious only after someone shows it to you. That is AI boom — a small key that opens a big door.
